svg.title: What the test of the connection checks
svg.desc: Test connection and save asks Paperless for one document. First Nextcloud has to reach Paperless at the URL: find its host, be allowed to connect to its address, connect within 3 seconds, trust its certificate and get an answer within 10 seconds; otherwise the message names which of these failed. Then Paperless has to answer with a status of 2xx; a refused token, a wrong path, a redirect or an error of the server each have their own message. Last, the answer has to be a list of documents of Paperless-ngx. Only then are the settings saved. Last, Paperless says what the account of the token may do, when it may view its UI settings, and the settings warn below the token about a superuser, an admin, an account that may change documents or one that may not view correspondents or document types, or those of the newest documents that another user owns.
